newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso softer on month-end dollar demand.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso softer on month-end dollar demand.

text.p: The Mexican peso extended initial weakness slightly by early trade on Monday due to month-end corporate demand to square dollar positions and sovereign bonds falling due, traders said.
"There is normal month-end demand for dollars to square positions," said a trader.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and the 24-hour contract were 3.75 and 3.8 centavos weaker, respectively, at 7.9140/7.9175 and 7.9090/7.9120 per dollar.
The same-day peso had meanwhile closed 6.05 centavos weaker at 7.9030/7.9080 per dollar.

"Debt maturity could also be putting the peso under some pressure," the trader added, referring to $1.5 billion in Cetes-Libor bonds issued by the Mexican government one year ago, whose payment may currently be under way.
Holders may chose between the highest of two rates, 12-month Libor or Cetes less 600 basis points, payable in dollars or pesos, respectively.
Traders situated support for the 48-hour peso at 7.9250 per dollar.
